reasoning: Emphatic ط as T, with a short i in the second syllable. The same consonants spell ruTab, fresh dates, but the adjective sense given here is raTib.
The long uu of a'uul shortens before the attached -lak, giving a'ullak, so the Arabic is respelled without the waw. shu and biddi are both Palestinian markers.
ق is a glottal stop and both vowels are short i, as in 'irift minno I got sick of him. Covers being fed up as much as physically disgusted.
Long ii in kariim. Said to close off worry about money or the future.
Form II participle, initial cluster mkh- and a shadda on the first ل. Used as a mass noun for pickles on the table, plural mkhallalaat.
ثاني is taani with t in Palestinian, hence the respelling. The Levantine calendar name used in Ramallah rather than nuufimbir.
ظ is written TH. This is the rural and Bedouin-flavoured variant; an urban Ramallah speaker usually says shu haad or shu haada.
ح is a moon letter so the article stays il-. The b- present feminine agrees with 7anafiyye, ق is a glottal stop and the shadda doubles it.
Final weak verb, he-form past, the water boiled. To boil something is the form II ghalla غلّى, which is what you hear more often in the kitchen.
jooz has a long oo and means husband here. Taa marbuta after the doubled م is e.
The final h is not heard, so it is said walla. Works as an oath, as emphasis, and as a questioning really.
The far demonstrative plural, against hadool for these. Two long vowels, uu then aa.
إذا is said iza, and عليك is 3aleek with a long ee, so both are respelled for the voice. ق in wa't is a glottal stop and ba- is the first person b- present.
khalli- plus -ni is the Palestinian let me. The subjunctive after khalliini takes no b-, and the feminine object is -ik.
Taa marbuta after ز is e. Strictly a she-goat; the plural is maa3iz or 3anzaat.
Initial cluster fr-, emphatic ط, and taa marbuta after an emphatic is a. Small change or coins, as in ma3ak fraaTa.
beet has a long ee, not ii. Literally may your house be ruined, but usually said half-admiringly rather than as a real curse.
ق is a glottal stop even in this set religious phrase, and the final hamza of البقاء is dropped in speech. Said on hearing of a death.
Emphatic ص, then a long aa, a y glide and ع before the final i. A skilled manual tradesman, often with a note of respect for the craft.
The shadda doubles ظ, which the scheme writes TH, and the initial mu- reduces to a cluster. Typically a salaried office or government employee.
il-7amdu lillah compresses to il-7amdilla in speech, so it is written as one run. maashi il-7aal is the standard modest answer to keef 7aalak.
Jussive-shaped blessing with no b- prefix, yi7faTH. ط in falasTiin is emphatic and ظ is written TH.
ذ comes out as z in this learned word, so it is respelled with ز. The pharyngeal ح blocks the raising of the taa marbuta, so a rather than e.
Form II with a shadda doubling the waw. In the search sense it takes 3ala: dawwar 3ala muftaa7o.
Long ii, and the word-initial hamza seat is not romanized. Feminine, and loosely covers the whole arm as well as the hand.
